notes: POC objective: validate Dedicated reserved GPU sizing to meet steady-state and burst SLOs for plant-edge assistants and nightly embedding jobs.

Representative workloads (confirmed):
 - Real-time operator chat (avg prompt 120 tokens, avg response 450 tokens) — target p95 <= 180ms for token generation after warm cache; concurrency target 60 concurrent sessions, 50 QPS sustained bursts up to 150 QPS for 30s.
- Embeddings pipeline for telemetry (batching allowed) — target throughput 15k embeddings/hour (~200 QPS) with batch sizes 32–64; cost sensitivity high for bulk nightly runs.
- Reranking for alert prioritization — short prompts, strict latency; p95 <= 120ms required for top-5 rerank.

Planned GPU footprint: initial reserved capacity proposal = 8x H100 (80GB) nodes with headroom for autoscaling to 12x for scheduled nightly jobs. Customer asked for guidance on model quantization (int8) vs accuracy tradeoffs.

Performance validation plan:
 - Synthetic load: Locust + Vegeta profiles mirroring peak patterns
 - Soak: 72h continuous run on Dedicated, monitor GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates, memory pressure
 - Stress: 5x burst tests to validate graceful degradation and fallback to smaller model variant
 - Regression: run canonical prompt set (200 prompts) each 6 hours, track embedding cosine drift and generation BLEU/ROUGE style signal for regressions
Observations so far: warm-cache p50/p95 vastly different immediately after deploy; prefix caching reduces token compute by ~22% in initial tests. Need to tune cache TTL and autoscaler thresholds.

SLA negotiation points raised by customer: credits for p95 breaches, per-route latency SLOs, guaranteed reserved GPU availability during scheduled campaigns, clear maintenance blackout windows, rollback windows for model upgrades.
Network/ops blockers: Verdant's on-prem to VPC egress bandwidth must sustain nightly embedding syncs; Ops asked for throughput numbers and example tcp/ip flows (we shared docs).
Security: must support SSO via SAML, audit log export to their SIEM, KMS integration with customer-owned keys, and 7-year retention for select audit logs (legal requirement).
